Parking the whole roadmap. Its two unfinished pieces are Track B's Stage 2 (closure notices, O5) and Track A's Ranked list (O2, O3, O4). Each becomes one deferred item. Stage 1's finding stays where it is.

**1. Read the item schema and the current backlog first**, so the items match the format and nothing already there gets overwritten:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/   (deferred-backlog reference: Deferred-item schema)
Read specs/deferred_items.md           (may not exist yet; if so, create it)
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`**, in the schema's exact field order and `Size:` scale. Each item stands on its own, so it can be picked up without reading the roadmap:

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices to boat operators (was Stage 2, Track B, O5)
      Boat operators get an email notice within an hour of a lock closing, by polling the closure log's live feed about every 10 minutes.
      Size: small
      Done when: a notice job and an operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (O2)
      Feed the river-level forecast through Stage 1's closure-response curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md: under 2% below 3.1 m, about 60% at 3.8 m) to get each lock's closure risk for the next 7 days.
      Size: small. One model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 minutes.
      Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock is produced from the river-level forecast.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled (O3)
      Fit a separate closure-vs-gauge curve for each of the 14 locks, pooled across locks. Stage 1 found that the four longest-record locks share nearly the same curve.
      Size: medium. About 14× Stage 1's data (about 25 GB vs 1.8 GB); compute unmeasured.
      Done when: a closure curve for each of the 14 locks, from a pooled fit, is recorded with the measured cost of its run.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (O4)
      A static map page showing each lock's closure history, for the canal's boat operators.
      Size: small. About a day of work.
      Done when: the closure-history map page exists and shows every lock's closure history.
```

**3. Retire the roadmap:**

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
```

Below its header, add:

> **PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete.** Funding for the canal study ended. Stage 2 and the Track A Ranked list (O2, O3, O4) are in `specs/deferred_items.md` under `## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06`.

This roadmap had no spec, methodology or critique files, so nothing else retires with it. The findings file stays in `specs/`, because the O2 and O3 items cite it.

**4. Commit on `main`:**

```
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete): funding ended; remaining work to deferred_items"
```

When this is done, the roadmap is closed and no stage gets handed off. The four items will age in the deferred backlog like any other items, and `/deferred` can promote any of them if funding or interest comes back.
